html:
Puerto Rico is a Caribbean island east of Hispaniola, a territory of the United States since 1898. The Taíno called it Borikén.

Columbus reached it in 1493, and Spain settled it in 1508. For four centuries it was a fortress colony guarding the sea lanes, with the great walls of San Juan. Sugar and coffee estates grew in the 1800s; slavery ended in 1873. Spain granted the island self-rule in 1897, but a year later the United States took it in the Spanish-American War.

Under the United States:

  • Puerto Ricans became US citizens in 1917, but they cannot vote for president while living on the island.
  • Pedro Albizu Campos led a nationalist movement for independence, which was harshly repressed.
  • Luis Muñoz Marín, the first elected governor, led Operation Bootstrap, a drive to industrialise, and the new Commonwealth status of 1952.
  • Hundreds of thousands moved to New York and other mainland cities after the Second World War.

Votes on whether to stay a territory, become a state or go independent have never settled the question. A debt crisis from 2016 and Hurricane Maria in 2017 hit the island hard. Like Cuba, it keeps a strong Spanish Caribbean culture.
sum: Puerto Rico is a Caribbean island east of Hispaniola, a territory of the United States since 1898. The Taíno called it Borikén.
